p.src: Now Zhong Jin and Zhong Shen barred Zhao Yun’s way and engaged him in battle. Zhao Yun leveled his spear and thrust at them. Zhong Jin came forward first, swinging his great axe to meet him. Their horses crossed, and before three bouts had passed, Zhao Yun thrust him from the saddle with a single stroke, then broke through and rode on. Zhong Shen pursued from behind with his halberd. As his horse pressed close upon Zhao Yun’s, the halberd’s point flickered continually at Zhao Yun’s back. Zhao Yun abruptly wheeled his horse, bringing the two riders breast to breast. With his left hand Zhao Yun used his spear to ward off the ornate halberd; with his right he drew the precious Qinggang sword and struck, cleaving away half of Zhong Shen’s helmet and skull. Zhong Shen fell dead from his horse, and the remaining troops scattered. Zhao Yun escaped and made for the Bridge of Changban. Then he heard a tremendous roar of shouting behind him. It was Wen Ping pursuing him at the head of his troops. By the time Zhao Yun reached the bridge, both man and horse were exhausted. Seeing Zhang Fei sitting his horse upon the bridge with spear leveled, Zhao Yun shouted, “Yide, come to my aid!” Zhang Fei replied, “Zilong, ride on quickly. I shall deal with the pursuers myself.”

p.src: Zhao Yun galloped across the bridge and, after riding more than twenty li, found Xuande and the others resting beneath some trees. He dismounted, prostrated himself, and wept. Xuande wept as well. Gasping for breath, Zhao Yun said, “Even ten thousand deaths would be too light a punishment for my crime! Lady Mi was gravely wounded and refused to mount the horse, so she threw herself into a well and died. I could only push down the earthen wall to cover her; then, carrying the young lord in my arms, I broke through the encircling ranks; and thanks to my lord’s great fortune, I was lucky enough to escape. Only a moment ago the young lord was still crying in my arms, but he has been silent and motionless for some time. I fear he may not have survived.” He thereupon loosened his armor to look. It turned out that Adou was sound asleep and had not yet awakened. Zhao Yun cried joyfully, “By good fortune, the young lord is unharmed!” He offered the child to Xuande with both hands. Xuande took the child and flung him to the ground, saying, “For the sake of an infant like you, I nearly lost one of my great generals!” Zhao Yun hastily picked Adou up from the ground, then wept and bowed, saying, “Even if I were to have my liver and brains smeared upon the earth, I could never repay your kindness!” A later poet wrote:

p.src: Meanwhile, Wen Ping pursued Zhao Yun to the Bridge of Changban. There he saw Zhang Fei, his tiger whiskers bristling and his great round eyes glaring, serpent spear in hand, sitting his horse upon the bridge; and behind the woods east of the bridge he saw great clouds of dust rising. Suspecting an ambush, he reined in and dared not approach.

p.src: Before long, Cao Ren, Li Dian, Xiahou Dun, Xiahou Yuan, Yue Jin, Zhang Liao, Zhang He, Xu Chu, and the rest all arrived. Seeing Zhang Fei glaring fiercely, spear held crosswise, sitting his horse upon the bridge, and fearing that this too was a stratagem of Zhuge Kongming, none dared advance. They halted their ranks and formed a line west of the bridge, then sent a swift messenger to report to Cao Cao. When Cao Cao heard the report, he swiftly mounted and came forward from the rear of the army. Zhang Fei opened his round eyes wide. In the distance he saw the blue silk parasol, yak-tail standards, axes, and banners of the rear army approaching, and guessed that Cao Cao, beset by doubts, had come in person to inspect the situation. Zhang Fei then thundered, “I am Zhang Yide of Yan! Who dares fight me to the death?” His voice was like a mighty thunderclap. When Cao Cao’s soldiers heard it, their legs all trembled. Cao Cao hastily ordered his parasol removed, then turned to those around him and said, “I once heard Yunchang say that Yide could take the head of an enemy commander amid an army of a million as easily as drawing an object from a bag. Now that we have met him today, we must not underestimate him.”

p.src: Before he had finished speaking, Zhang Fei glared again and shouted, “Zhang Yide of Yan is here! Who dares come and fight me to the death?” Seeing Zhang Fei’s imposing spirit, Cao Cao began to think of retreat. Zhang Fei saw Cao Cao’s rear ranks begin to shift, so he leveled his spear and shouted once more, “You will neither fight nor retreat—what is the meaning of this?”

p.src: Before the shout had died away, Xiahou Jie at Cao Cao’s side was so terrified that his courage failed him, and he toppled from his horse. Cao Cao wheeled his horse and fled. At once, all the troops and generals fled westward together. Indeed: How could a yellow-beaked child bear the sound of a thunderbolt? How could a sickly woodcutter endure the roar of tigers and leopards? For a time, those who cast away their spears and dropped their helmets were beyond counting. Men surged like a tide and horses tumbled like collapsing mountains, trampling one another underfoot. A later poet wrote:

p.src: Now Cao Cao, terrified by Zhang Fei’s might, galloped westward. His cap pins all fell away, and he fled with his hair streaming loose. Zhang Liao and Xu Chu caught up and seized his reins. Cao Cao was utterly flustered and at a loss. Zhang Liao said, “Prime Minister, do not be alarmed. Zhang Fei is only one man; why fear him so greatly? If we turn our army back and attack at once, Liu Bei can be captured.” Only then did Cao Cao’s composure somewhat return. He ordered Zhang Liao and Xu Chu to go back to the Bridge of Changban and learn what had happened.

p.src: Meanwhile, when Zhang Fei saw Cao Cao’s army retreat in a mass, he dared not pursue. He quickly recalled the twenty-odd horsemen who had accompanied him, had them remove the branches tied to their horses’ tails, and ordered the bridge torn down. Then he rode back to Xuande and gave a full account of how he had destroyed it. Xuande said, “My brother, brave though you are, regrettably you have fallen short in calculation.” Zhang Fei asked why. Xuande said, “Cao Cao is full of schemes. You should not have destroyed the bridge. He will surely pursue us now.” Zhang Fei said, “One shout from me drove him back several li. How would he dare pursue us again?” Xuande said, “Had you left the bridge intact, he would have feared an ambush and dared not advance; but now that you have destroyed it, he will judge from our timidity that we have no troops, and he will certainly pursue. He commands a million men; even the Yangzi and Han rivers could be filled in for them to cross. How could he fear the loss of a single bridge?” They therefore set out at once, taking a side path toward Hanjin and making for the road to Mianyang.

p.src: Meanwhile, Cao Cao sent Zhang Liao and Xu Chu to investigate the Bridge of Changban. They returned and reported, “Zhang Fei has torn down the bridge and gone.” Cao Cao said, “He destroyed the bridge before leaving because he was afraid.” He thereupon ordered ten thousand troops to build three pontoon bridges with all speed, declaring that the army must cross that very night. Li Dian said, “I fear this may be one of Zhuge Liang’s deceptive schemes. We must not advance rashly.” Cao Cao said, “Zhang Fei is merely a man of brute courage. How could he devise such a scheme?” He then sent down orders for the army to advance with all possible speed.

p.src: Meanwhile, as Xuande approached Hanjin, he suddenly saw great clouds of dust rising behind him, while drums resounded to the heavens and battle cries shook the earth. Xuande said, “A great river lies before us, and pursuing troops are behind us. What are we to do?” He hastily ordered Zhao Yun to prepare to meet the enemy. Cao Cao issued an order to his army: “Liu Bei is now a fish in the cauldron, a tiger in the pit; if we do not capture him now, it will be like releasing a fish into the sea or letting a tiger return to the mountains. All commanders, press forward with every effort.” The commanders received the order and, each displaying his valor, pressed the pursuit. Suddenly drums sounded behind a hillside, and a body of horse and foot burst forth, shouting, “I have been waiting here for you a long time!”

p.src: At their head rode a great commander wielding the Green Dragon blade and mounted upon the Red Hare. It was none other than Guan Yunchang. He had gone to Jiangxia and secured ten thousand troops and horses; learning of the great battle at Changban near Dangyang, he had come expressly to intercept the enemy along this road. The moment Cao Cao saw Yunchang, he reined in, turned to his commanders, and said, “We have fallen into another of Zhuge Liang’s schemes!” He gave orders for the main army to retreat at once.

p.src: While they were speaking, the thunder of war drums suddenly arose from the southern bank of the river, and ships innumerable as ants came sailing before the wind. Xuande was greatly alarmed. When the vessels drew near, a man in a white robe and silver armor could be seen standing at the prow and calling aloud, “Uncle, have you been well since we parted? Your unworthy nephew has sinned by arriving too late!” Xuande looked and saw that it was Liu Qi. p.src: Xuande was delighted. The forces united, and they discussed how Cao Cao might be defeated. Kongming said, “Xiakou is strongly situated and has ample money and provisions, so it can be held for a long time. I ask my lord to station himself at Xiakou. Let the young lord return to Jiangxia, put the warships in order, and prepare the weapons. With the two positions supporting each other like horns, we can withstand Cao Cao. If we all return to Jiangxia, our position will instead be isolated.” Liu Qi said, “The military adviser’s words are excellent. Yet my humble wish is to invite my uncle to Jiangxia for a while. Once the troops and horses are properly settled, it will not be too late for him to return to Xiakou.” Xuande said, “My worthy nephew’s words are also sound.” Accordingly, he left Yunchang with five thousand troops to defend Xiakou. Xuande, Kongming, and Liu Qi went together to Jiangxia.

p.src: Now Cao Cao, seeing Yunchang lead troops out to intercept him on the overland route, suspected an ambush and dared not pursue. Fearing also that Xuande might reach Jiangling first by water, he hurried his army toward Jiangling through the night. Deng Yi, the administrative aide of Jingzhou, and Liu Xian, its assistant administrator, already knew all that had happened at Xiangyang. Judging that they could not resist Cao Cao, they led the soldiers and people of Jingzhou out of the city to surrender.

p.src: Cao Cao entered the city and, after restoring order among the people, released Han Song from prison and promoted him to Grand Herald. All the other officials likewise received titles and rewards. Cao Cao consulted his generals, saying, “Liu Bei has now gone to Jiangxia. I fear that he will ally himself with Eastern Wu and become an ever-growing menace. What plan should we use to destroy him?” Xun You said, “Now that our military might stands at its height, we should send an envoy bearing a proclamation to Jiangdong, inviting Sun Quan to join us in a hunt at Jiangxia, capture Liu Bei together, divide the lands of Jingzhou, and bind ourselves in lasting alliance. Sun Quan will surely grow fearful and suspicious and come to submit; then our purpose will be accomplished.”

p.src: Cao Cao adopted his plan, sending forth the proclamation and dispatching an envoy to Eastern Wu, while on the other hand he mustered a total of eight hundred and thirty thousand cavalry, infantry, and marines, falsely claiming a million. They advanced by land and water, ships and horsemen moving abreast along the river. Their camps and stockades stretched in an unbroken chain for more than three hundred li, from the Jing Gorges in the west to Qi and Huang in the east.

p.src: The story now divides. Meanwhile Sun Quan of Jiangdong had stationed his troops in Chaisang Commandery. Hearing that Cao Cao’s great army had reached Xiangyang, that Liu Cong had surrendered, and that Cao Cao was now hastening day and night by forced marches to seize Jiangling, he assembled his advisers to discuss a plan of defense. Lu Su said, “Jingzhou borders our realm. Its rivers and mountains make it naturally secure, and its people are numerous and prosperous. If we take and hold it, it will provide the foundation for an imperial enterprise. Now Liu Biao has only just died and Liu Bei has only just been defeated. I ask leave to go to Jiangxia under orders to offer condolences and, taking that occasion, persuade Liu Bei to pacify Liu Biao’s generals and unite with them wholeheartedly to defeat Cao Cao. If Liu Bei gladly complies, our great undertaking can succeed.” Sun Quan gladly accepted his proposal and at once sent Lu Su with condolence gifts to Jiangxia.

p.src: Meanwhile Xuande reached Jiangxia and discussed a sound plan with Kongming and Liu Qi. Kongming said, “Cao Cao’s power is great, and it will be difficult to resist him at once. We would do better to seek the support of Sun Quan of Eastern Wu. Let north and south hold each other in check while we reap the advantage between them. Why should we not?” Xuande said, “Jiangdong has a great many men of talent, and they must have far-reaching designs. How could they be willing to accept us?” Kongming laughed and said, “Now Cao Cao has brought a host of a million and crouches like a tiger over the Jiang and Han rivers. How could Jiangdong fail to send someone to discover the truth of the situation? When someone arrives, I shall borrow a favoring wind and sail straight to Jiangdong; with this ever-ready three-inch tongue of mine, I shall persuade the armies of north and south to devour each other. If the southern army wins, we shall join it in destroying Cao Cao and take the lands of Jingzhou. If the northern army wins, we may seize the opportunity to take Jiangnan.” Xuande said, “That is a most profound argument. But how are we to bring someone from Jiangdong here?”

When someone arrives, I shall borrow a favoring wind and sail straight to Jiangdong; with this ever-ready three-inch tongue of mine, I shall persuade the armies of north and south to devour each other.
If the southern army wins, we shall join it in destroying Cao Cao and take the lands of Jingzhou.
If the northern army wins, we may seize the opportunity to take Jiangnan.”
Xuande said, “That is a most profound argument.
But how are we to bring someone from Jiangdong here?”

p.src: While they were speaking, a messenger reported that Sun Quan of Jiangdong had sent Lu Su to offer condolences and that his ship had already reached the bank. Kongming laughed and said, “Our great enterprise will succeed!” He then asked Liu Qi, “When Sun Ce died, did Xiangyang send anyone to offer condolences?” Liu Qi replied, “Jiangdong bears a blood feud against our house for the killing of a father. How could we exchange the courtesies of celebration and mourning?” Kongming said, “Then Lu Su has come not to offer condolences, but to sound out our military situation.” He then said to Xuande, “When Lu Su arrives, if he asks about Cao Cao’s movements, my lord need only profess ignorance. If he asks again and again, simply tell him that he may ask Zhuge Liang.”

p.src: Their plan settled, they sent men to welcome Lu Su. Lu Su entered the city and offered his condolences. After the gifts had been received, Liu Qi invited him to meet Xuande. When the formalities were complete, he was invited into the rear hall for wine. Lu Su said, “I have long heard the great name of the Imperial Uncle but have never had occasion to pay my respects. Now that I am fortunate enough to meet you, it is truly a comfort. I recently heard that the Imperial Uncle fought Cao Cao, so you must know the true state of his forces. May I ask approximately how many troops Cao Cao has?” Xuande said, “My troops are few and my generals scarce. The moment I heard Cao Cao had arrived, I fled, and so I know nothing of the true state of his forces.” Lu Su said, “I heard that, using Zhuge Kongming’s stratagems, the Imperial Uncle twice attacked with fire and frightened Cao Cao out of his wits. How can you say you know nothing?” Xuande said, “Only by asking Kongming can you learn the details.” Lu Su asked, “Where is Kongming? I should like to meet him.”

p.src: Xuande ordered that Kongming be invited out to meet him. After Lu Su and Kongming had exchanged courtesies, Lu Su said, “I have long admired your talent and virtue, sir, but have never had the honor of meeting you. Now that fortune has brought us together, I should like to hear your view of the present dangers and prospects.” Kongming said, “I fully understand Cao Cao’s treacherous designs. I regret only that our strength is insufficient, and so for the present we have withdrawn before him.” Lu Su asked, “Does the Imperial Uncle intend to remain here now?” Kongming replied, “My lord has an old friendship with Wu Chen, the governor of Cangwu, and intends to seek refuge with him.” Lu Su said, “Wu Chen has little grain and few troops and cannot even protect himself. How could he shelter another?” Kongming said, “Though Wu Chen’s territory is no place to remain for long, we shall rely on him for the present while pursuing another sound design.”

p.src: Lu Su said, “General Sun holds the six commanderies with the might of a tiger. His troops are elite, his provisions abundant, and he shows the utmost respect for worthy and learned men; thus the heroes of Jiangdong have rallied to him in great numbers. For your sake, the best course would be to send a trusted confidant to form an alliance with Eastern Wu, so that together you may pursue a great enterprise.” Kongming said, “Liu Bei and General Sun have never had any former friendship, so I fear that words would be spent in vain. Besides, there is no trusted confidant whom we can send.” Lu Su said, “Your elder brother, sir, now serves as an adviser in Jiangdong and longs daily to see you. Though I am a man of little talent, I am willing to accompany you to see General Sun and discuss our great undertaking together.” Xuande said, “Kongming is my teacher; I cannot bear to be parted from him even for an instant. How can he go?”

I beg leave to obey the summons and make the journey.” Only then did Xuande consent. Lu Su then took leave of Xuande and Liu Qi, boarded a boat with Kongming, and set out for Chaisang Commandery.
